sub_graphs.title: Tangerine Whistle: I/O Operation Gas Repricing
sub_graphs.description: Models the gas cost changes for I/O-intensive operations introduced to prevent DoS attacks (EIP-150)

nodes.label: Opcode Execution Pending
nodes.description: System state when an I/O-intensive opcode is about to execute

nodes.label: Check Tangerine Whistle Gas Cost
nodes.description: Look up the new gas cost for the opcode under Tangerine Whistle rules

nodes.label: Deduct Increased Gas Cost
nodes.description: Subtract the higher gas cost from available gas (CALL: 40->700, BALANCE: 20->400, EXTCODESIZE: 20->700, etc.)

nodes.label: Gas Sufficient for Operation
nodes.description: Available gas is sufficient to cover the increased cost

nodes.label: Out of Gas
nodes.description: Increased gas cost exceeds available gas, triggering out-of-gas exception

nodes.label: Execute I/O Operation
nodes.description: Perform the actual I/O operation (state access, external call, etc.)

nodes.label: I/O Operation Completed
nodes.description: I/O operation successfully completed with new gas pricing

edges.label: Look up Tangerine Whistle gas cost

external_entities.name: EVM Interpreter
external_entities.description: The Ethereum Virtual Machine interpreter executing contract bytecode

sub_graphs.title: Tangerine Whistle: CALL Gas Stipend Rules
sub_graphs.description: Models the 63/64 gas rule for CALL operations introduced in EIP-150

nodes.label: CALL Operation Initiated
nodes.description: System state when a CALL/DELEGATECALL/CALLCODE is about to execute

nodes.label: Compute Available Gas for Call
nodes.description: Calculate gas available: min(requested_gas, current_gas - current_gas/64)

nodes.label: Gas Capped at 63/64
nodes.description: Gas forwarded to child call is limited to 63/64 of remaining gas

nodes.label: Execute Child Call
nodes.description: Execute the called contract with capped gas allowance

nodes.label: Child Execution Complete
nodes.description: Child call finished, return unused gas to caller

nodes.label: Return Unused Gas to Caller
nodes.description: Add remaining gas from child call back to caller's gas counter

nodes.label: Gas Refunded to Caller
nodes.description: Caller has received unused gas from child call

edges.label: Enter child context with capped gas

external_entities.name: Calling Contract
external_entities.description: Smart contract executing a CALL/DELEGATECALL/CALLCODE operation

sub_graphs.title: Tangerine Whistle: SELFDESTRUCT Gas Increase
sub_graphs.description: Models the increased gas cost for SELFDESTRUCT operation to prevent DoS via mass destructions

nodes.label: SELFDESTRUCT Requested
nodes.description: System state when SELFDESTRUCT opcode is encountered

nodes.label: Check if Beneficiary is New Account
nodes.description: Determine if SELFDESTRUCT sends to a new (non-existent) account

nodes.label: Beneficiary Account Exists
nodes.description: Target account already exists in state trie

nodes.label: Beneficiary is New Account
nodes.description: Target account does not exist, will be created

nodes.label: Deduct Base SELFDESTRUCT Gas
nodes.description: Deduct increased base cost (0 -> 5000 gas)

nodes.label: Deduct New Account Creation Gas
nodes.description: Deduct additional 25000 gas for new account creation

nodes.label: Execute SELFDESTRUCT
nodes.description: Transfer balance and mark contract for deletion

nodes.label: Contract Marked for Destruction
nodes.description: Contract balance transferred and marked for deletion at end of transaction

edges.label: Add 25000 gas for new account (if applicable)

ambiguities.text: The index page only shows file structure without specific gas cost values.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Use known EIP-150 values: CALL/EXTCODESIZE/EXTCODECOPY: 20->700, BALANCE: 20->400, SLOAD: 50->200, SELFDESTRUCT: 0->5000, new account creation: 25000.

ambiguities.text: Exact behavior of 63/64 rule when requested gas exceeds available gas is not detailed.
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume min(requested_gas, available_gas - available_gas/64) formula applies, capping at maximum passable gas.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers could previously exploit low gas costs for I/O operations to perform DoS attacks on the network.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If the previous gas costs were not actually exploitable, the repricing introduces unnecessary cost increases for legitimate contracts.

implicit_assumptions.description: Existing contracts may have been written assuming the old gas costs and may run out of gas after the fork.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Contracts that still work after repricing are unaffected, but those that relied on low gas costs will break.

implicit_assumptions.description: The 63/64 rule provides sufficient gas for the caller to handle return values and continue execution.
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If 1/64 is insufficient for post-call handling, contracts could fail unexpectedly after successful child calls.
